claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s after matching (accepted 14:05:00, cancelled 14:07:55) — she was not in a position to cancel free of charge under NS-4, which only exempts cancels made within 3 minutes of matching.

The $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F5) is a rider-side cancellation charge and no surge applies (F6), so the amount disputed is exactly the published $6.61 and cannot be reduced on any fare ground.

The rider's fee is only chargeable if the driver completed the NS-1 conditions (press "I'm Here", be within GPS range of the pickup, wait over 3 minutes); on the record the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival was recorded (F4), and no arrival was recorded at the pickup at all (F3), so NS-1 (i)-(iii) are not met.

System GPS places the driver 2189 m from the pickup at the moment of cancellation and never within 200 m (F1); the driver's own statement that he was "on my way" (F10) is consistent with this but is a statement only and cannot outweigh the GPS record.

The 3-minute waiting condition in NS-1 (iii) is arithmetically impossible here: the whole trip from acceptance to cancellation lasted 2 min 55 s (F2), which is less than the required >3:01 continuous wait at the pickup.

The driver's chat message "5 min more, traffic is slow" (F8) shows he was still en route and ETA-pending at 14:06, corroborating that he had not arrived and had not begun any waiting period before the rider cancelled; the chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F9).

Traffic facts show only a category-2 speed band of 30–39 km/h on Stevens Road (F11) with no incidents recorded near the route (F12) and fair weather (F13); this does not justify the driver's distance from the pickup, so I do not contest NS-2 on that basis and instead rely on the timeline and GPS records.

The driver has 1460 days of account history, a 4.77 rating, 652 trips in 90 days and zero disputes or upheld complaints in that window (F15); this supports that the failure to reach the pickup was an isolated service shortfall rather than a pattern, and I ask that no account flag be attached.

weaknesses: F1 and F3 are decisive against the driver: GPS shows he was 2189 m away and never within 200 m, and no arrival was ever recorded, so NS-1 (i)-(ii) plainly fail and the $6.61 cannot be sustained.
The driver's statement F10 ("I was on my way when the rider cancelled") is contradicted by the GPS record F1 for any claim of proximity, so it cannot be used to argue he was at or near the pickup.

The driver's own message F8 ("5 min more") concedes he was going to be roughly 5 minutes late beyond the rider's 14:05 enquiry, which supports the rider's account that the driver was nowhere near and weakens any argument that the short 2 min 55 s window was unfair to the driver.

The rider's complaint timeline is corroborated by system records F1-F4, and F14 shows the rider has one dispute in 90 days with none upheld, so there is no profile basis to attack the complaint's credibility.

The fare facts F5/F6 establish only that $6.61 was charged with no surge; they do not create any entitlement to the fee absent NS-1, so the driver has no affirmative fare argument to fall back on if NS-1 fails.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.97)
events.body:
The booking was an instant on-demand RydeX trip cancelled by the rider: F2 records acceptance at 14:05:00 and rider cancellation at 14:07:55, i.e. 175 s (2 min 55 s) after matching. Under NS-0 the rider-cancellation branch of an instant booking is governed by NS-4, which makes all cancellations made within 3 minutes of matching non-chargeable [F2][NS-0][NS-4]. The 175 s interval is inside that 3:00 window, so the $6.61 cancellation fee recorded in F5 was not chargeable and must be returned in full [F2][F5][NS-4].

The alternative driver no-show route to charging the fee also fails on the record. The driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival (F4), and no arrival at the pickup was ever recorded at all (F3), so NS-1(i) is not met [F3][F4][NS-1]. GPS places the driver 2189 m from the pickup at the moment of cancellation and never within 200 m (F1), so NS-1(ii) is not met either [F1][NS-1]. And the entire span from acceptance to cancellation was only 2 min 55 s (F2), less than the continuous waiting period NS-1(iii) requires, so no waiting clock ever started [F2][NS-1]. Any of these failures is sufficient to require full refund under NS-2 [F1][F3][F4][NS-2].

The driver's chat message at 14:06 ("5 min more, traffic is slow") confirms he was still en route about a minute before the cancellation, and the chat record is complete with two timestamped messages, so the timeline and GPS records are reliable and no G12 evidence gap arises [F7][F8][F9][NS-1]. The only congestion evidence is a category-2 band 4 (30–39 km/h) record on Stevens Road with no incidents near the route and fair weather, which does not meet the RD-4 traffic-evidence requirement and is not needed here in any event [F11][F12][F13][RD-4]. what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching, NS-4 would have upheld the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s after matching (accepted 14:05:00, cancelled 14:07:55), which is within the 3-minute grace window, so no cancellation fee is chargeable at all.
This was an instant (on-demand) booking cancelled by the rider, so it falls under NS-0's rider-cancellation branch (NS-4), not the driver-claims-no-show branch.
Even on the driver's no-show theory the fee cannot stand: the driver never came within 200 m of the pickup point, his closest approach being 2189 m at the moment of cancellation, so NS-1(ii) fails.
The platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point and no arrival confirmation exists — the driver never tapped "I'm Here" — so NS-1(i) also fails and no 3-minute waiting clock ever started.
The driver's own message at 14:06 saying "5 min more, traffic is slow" corroborates that he had not arrived at 14:06, one minute before the rider cancelled.

The only recorded congestion was a moderate band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Stevens Road and no incidents were recorded, so the driver's "traffic is slow" remark does not amount to the reasonable-cause traffic evidence RD-4 requires.
The $6.61 cancellation fee was in fact charged and must be refunded in full because the statutory conditions for charging it are not met.
The chat record is complete with two timestamped messages, so the timeline and GPS records are reliable and no G12 evidence-gap referral is needed.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint says the driver "was nowhere near", but the only hard support for that is the GPS fact F1 (2189 m) — if the judge reads F1 as the fixed position at cancellation only, the rider cannot show where the driver was earlier in the 3-minute window.

The driver's written statement F10 ("I was on my way when the rider cancelled") is not contradicted by any system record of arrival, but a judge could still read it as a benign explanation rather than any breach on his part.

The rider's own profile (F14: rating 4.3, 1 dispute in 90 d) is thin and gives the rider no clean-record advantage over the driver (F15: rating 4.77, 652 trips, 0 disputes), so no supplementary flag_account or credibility bonus is available to the rider.

If the judge were to treat the booking as an advanced booking (which the fact index does not support), NS-5 rather than NS-4 would apply; the rider relies on the stated instant-booking, 2 min 55 s cancellation in F2.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s after matching (accepted 14:05:00, cancelled 14:07:55) — she was not in a position to cancel free of charge under NS-4, which only exempts cancels made within 3 minutes of matching.

The $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F5) is a rider-side cancellation charge and no surge applies (F6), so the amount disputed is exactly the published $6.61 and cannot be reduced on any fare ground.

The rider's fee is only chargeable if the driver completed the NS-1 conditions (press "I'm Here", be within GPS range of the pickup, wait over 3 minutes); on the record the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival was recorded (F4), and no arrival was recorded at the pickup at all (F3), so NS-1 (i)-(iii) are not met.

System GPS places the driver 2189 m from the pickup at the moment of cancellation and never within 200 m (F1); the driver's own statement that he was "on my way" (F10) is consistent with this but is a statement only and cannot outweigh the GPS record.

The 3-minute waiting condition in NS-1 (iii) is arithmetically impossible here: the whole trip from acceptance to cancellation lasted 2 min 55 s (F2), which is less than the required >3:01 continuous wait at the pickup.

The driver's chat message "5 min more, traffic is slow" (F8) shows he was still en route and ETA-pending at 14:06, corroborating that he had not arrived and had not begun any waiting period before the rider cancelled; the chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F9).

Traffic facts show only a category-2 speed band of 30–39 km/h on Stevens Road (F11) with no incidents recorded near the route (F12) and fair weather (F13); this does not justify the driver's distance from the pickup, so I do not contest NS-2 on that basis and instead rely on the timeline and GPS records.

The driver has 1460 days of account history, a 4.77 rating, 652 trips in 90 days and zero disputes or upheld complaints in that window (F15); this supports that the failure to reach the pickup was an isolated service shortfall rather than a pattern, and I ask that no account flag be attached.

weaknesses: F1 and F3 are decisive against the driver: GPS shows he was 2189 m away and never within 200 m, and no arrival was ever recorded, so NS-1 (i)-(ii) plainly fail and the $6.61 cannot be sustained.
The driver's statement F10 ("I was on my way when the rider cancelled") is contradicted by the GPS record F1 for any claim of proximity, so it cannot be used to argue he was at or near the pickup.

The driver's own message F8 ("5 min more") concedes he was going to be roughly 5 minutes late beyond the rider's 14:05 enquiry, which supports the rider's account that the driver was nowhere near and weakens any argument that the short 2 min 55 s window was unfair to the driver.

The rider's complaint timeline is corroborated by system records F1-F4, and F14 shows the rider has one dispute in 90 days with none upheld, so there is no profile basis to attack the complaint's credibility.

The fare facts F5/F6 establish only that $6.61 was charged with no surge; they do not create any entitlement to the fee absent NS-1, so the driver has no affirmative fare argument to fall back on if NS-1 fails.

Adopted, not contested: D3 concedes that NS-1(i)–(iii) are unmet on F3 and F4, which is exactly the rider's C3/C4 — the driver's no-show branch fails, so the fee cannot be sustained under NS-1.
Adopted: D4 concedes F1 puts the driver 2189 m away and never within 200 m, which is the rider's own strongest fact under NS-1(ii) and confirms no valid no-show charge exists.

Adopted: F8 and F9 confirm the driver was still en route at 14:06 and that the record is complete, which removes any G12 evidence-gap argument and leaves the rider's NS-4 free-cancel right intact.
Adopted: F11–F13 show no qualifying congestion or incident, so RD-4 gives the driver no justification and D7 itself abandons that basis; the rider's refund claim stands on NS-4 and NS-2.

Conceded. F1 places the driver 2189 m from the pickup at the moment of cancellation and never within 200 m, so NS-1(ii) fails and NS-2 requires the fee to be returned; my client does not contest the refund.
Conceded. F4 records no 'I'm Here' tap and no automatic arrival, and F3 records no arrival at all, so NS-1(i) fails and no 3-minute waiting clock ever started.

Not contested on arrival, but F8 is my client's own message and cuts both ways: it shows he was still en route and ETA-pending at 14:06, which is why I do not ask the court to sustain the fee — it does not make the fee chargeable.

Not contested. F11 shows only a category-2 band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Stevens Road, F12 records no incidents near the route and F13 fair weather, so the driver's 'traffic is slow' remark is not the traffic evidence the policy requires; this point is correct and I do not rely on it.

Conceded as to the $6.61 itself: F5 records the fee and NS-2 requires full refund of $6.61 because NS-1 (i)-(iii) all fail on F1, F3 and F4; the refund should issue as a voucher per NS-7, which is a formality, not a reduction.

Not contested — F9 shows 2 messages, all timestamped, and F7/F8 are consistent with the timeline, so the system records govern and no G12 referral is needed; I flag only that this completeness likewise forecloses any rider-side argument that the driver's absence is unproven.

Withdrawn to the extent it sought to resist a refund; I maintain only that F15 (1460-day account, 4.77 rating, 652 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes) shows this was an isolated service shortfall and is a reason not to attach any flag_account to my client.
